capitals.name: Pskov
capitals.note: Coordinates 57 49 N 28 20 E (Pskov page); 'the city became capital of the newly independent Pskov Republic' in 1348. Before 1348 it was the seat of Dovmont and of the princes Pskov invited.

keyframe_review.note: 22,601 km2 for 1285-1421, 108 grid cells around Pskov, Izborsk, Gdov, Ostrov and Pechory. The page gives no area and says only that the territory 'was roughly equivalent to modern-day Pskov Oblast'; the Oblast is 268 grid cells, so the shape is 0.40 of it, beyond the factor of two. The shape is kept, not the page's loose phrase: Cliopatria draws the rest of the Oblast inside its Novgorod (about 66 cells) and Lithuanian (73-93 cells) shapes, and no page opened gives a boundary (the Pskov page has no borders either). Cliopatria's Novgorod shape of 1236-1240 contains this land and nothing covers it in 1241-1284; the Pskov row begins in 1285.

21,734 km2: the same cells as 1422 (108 km2 less in polygon terms). No page dates a change in 1440; none is claimed.

region.text: Pskov, Izborsk, Gdov, Ostrov and Pechory: Cliopatria's first Pskov shape

ledger.note: 1285: Pskov stands apart from Novgorod, as Cliopatria draws it. The page is silent on 1285; it says that under Dovmont (prince of Pskov 1266-1299) 'Pskov asserted greater political autonomy and achieved de facto independence from Novgorod', while Novgorod still claimed authority (Yaroslav's interference in 1270). The Bolotovo page: 'de facto independent for perhaps a century before 1348'.

1348: the Treaty of Bolotovo recognises Pskov's independence from Novgorod; Pskov becomes the Pskov Republic. 'The Treaty of Bolotovo ... was concluded in 1348 between ... Novgorod the Great and Pskov'; it 'recognized Pskov's political independence from Novgorod'. Valentin Yanin argues for 1329; the Pskov Republic page gives 1348 as the traditional date and a scholarly range of 1329-1342. The land does not change.

region.text: the two cells of the 1285 shape that are not in the 1422 shape (Estonian-Latvian fringe)

ledger.note: 1422: two fringe cells (now in Estonia and Latvia) pass to the Livonian Conference. No page dates it; Cliopatria's Pskov shape loses them in 1422, when its Livonian Conference row begins, and that row covers both cells.

January 1510: Moscow annexes Pskov. 'The veche bell was removed' on 13 January 1510; Vasili arrived on 24 January and 'treated it as his father had treated Novgorod in 1478', resettling about 300 leading families; 'Vasili annexed the republic of Pskov in 1510'. The Pskov Republic page infobox: disestablished 1510, succeeded by the Grand Principality of Moscow.
January 1510: the Pskov Republic ends, annexed by Vasily III.

wars.name: Livonian siege of Pskov (1299)
wars.outcome: 'On 4 March 1299, the Livonian Order unexpectedly invaded north-western Russia and laid siege to Pskov'; Dovmont defeated them again after a battle on the Velikaya River and died on 20 May 1299 in a plague. No land changed hands.

wars.name: Lithuanian-Muscovite border war over Pskov
wars.outcome: 'Lithuania attacks Pskov, and Moscow sends troops, starting a border war that lasts until 1408'; no territorial result on the page.

wars.name: Muscovite-Livonian war of 1501-1503
wars.outcome: Pskov and Moscow forces lost the Battle of the Siritsa River to the Livonian Order in 1501; a six-year truce followed in summer 1503. No land changed hands on the page.

wars.name: Moscow's annexation of Pskov
wars.outcome: Vasily III, in Novgorod in 1509, summoned Pskov's representatives, accused the Pskovites at Epiphany 1510, had the veche bell removed on 13 January and entered Pskov on 24 January 1510; Pskov was annexed without battle.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary: the Pskov page names only neighbours (Novgorod, Lithuania, the Livonian Order) and a 1417 peace treaty with the Order, and the 1503 truce, without lines. The Peipus-Pskov lake shore is the one natural frontier, on the west.

notes:
START. Cliopatria's Pskov row begins in 1285, when its Novgorod row resumes after a gap (no Novgorod shape for 1241-1284; the Novgorod shape of 1236-1240 contains the Pskov core). The found event is confidence 1 because no page dates 1285. The pages give other starting points: 1228-1242 a first period of self-declared independence ended by the Livonian Order (Pskov Republic page; the Pskov page has the Teutonic Knights take the town in 1241 and Alexander Nevsky retake it months later), 1266 Dovmont prince and de facto independence (Daumantas page), 1329 (Yanin) or 1348 (traditional; Treaty of Bolotovo, Pskov Republic infobox) formal independence. The dossier follows Cliopatria to avoid double-drawing against the Novgorod 1241-1284 gap-fill that batch eu-16-b may write: if that fill includes the Pskov core, remove it from 1266 to 1284 there or start Pskov at 1266 here.

NOT IN THE LEDGER (suzerainty belongs to the other side's dossier, which has the vassal event types): Lithuania (the Pskov page: the city recognised Lithuanian overlordship in 1341 and returned to Novgorod in 1347; the Pskov Republic page: Pskov cut ties with Algirdas and Andrei of Polotsk in April 1349; Dovmont himself was a Lithuanian prince): a vassal_start/vassal_end for grand-duchy-of-lithuania with counterpart pskov-republic, 1341-1349 (years differ by page). Moscow (the Pskov Republic page: in 1399 Pskov asked Moscow for a prince and its princes became Moscow's viceroys; 1449 treaties 'recognize Pskov as a Moscow dependency'; 1462 and 1467 governor and deputies; 1494 Ivan III's treaty with Lithuania 'calls Pskov his patrimony'; 1499 Vasili given the title of grand prince of Novgorod and Pskov): grand-principality-of-moscow should record a vassal_start pskov-republic from 1399 (or 1449) to 1510.

AREA. The page gives no km2; the only measure is 'roughly equivalent to modern-day Pskov Oblast'. Cliopatria's shape is 0.40 of the Oblast's grid cells; kept (see the 1285 keyframe). The 1440, 1475, 1482 and 1507 shapes have the same cells as 1422; their area differences (108 km2) are polygon artefacts.

PAGE BUDGET 5 of 5 used (Pskov Republic, Treaty of Bolotovo, Daumantas of Pskov, Vasily III of Russia, Pskov). No page failed. The ruler strip is omitted: the princes' table on the Pskov Republic page is partial and overlapping (Andrei of Polotsk 1342-1349, again 1377-1399; Ivan Andreyevich 1386-1394).
